review.summary: AGENTLESS presents a deliberately simple repository-repair pipeline—hierarchical code localization followed by sampled patch generation, regression-test filtering, and majority voting—and shows that this design can perform competitively on SWE-bench Lite at low reported inference cost. Its useful additional contribution is a manual classification of benchmark problems and a filtered 252-problem variant, though comparative claims remain bounded by the benchmark and by reliance on reported baseline results.

observations.claim: The method is clearly specified as a practical two-stage system, and combines localization with patch selection rather than relying on autonomous tool-use planning.
observations.quote: AGENTLESS solves repository-level issues using a simple step-by-step procedure.

observations.claim: On the original benchmark, the paper reports 82 resolved problems (27.33%) at $0.34 average cost; its ablations indicate gains from multi-sampling/voting and test filtering.
observations.quote: Finally, the fullAGENTLESS performance is achieved by further applying filtering to select only the patches which can successfully pass the existing regressions tests.

observations.claim: The authors identify concrete benchmark-quality concerns and provide a filtered evaluation set; AGENTLESS resolves 71/252 (28.17%) there.
observations.quote: We refer to our subset of 252 problems as SWE-bench Lite-S.

observations.claim: Comparisons on the filtered set are not fully controlled: the authors could not rerun commercial systems on it, so their outcomes derive from excluding cases in prior reported results.
observations.quote: as we are not able to run commercial tools ourselves on the modified problems, we simply exclude the problematic problems in the below evaluation.

unresolved_questions: How robust are the reported rankings and cost advantages across other repository-level benchmarks, model versions, and independently rerun baselines?
Would the filtered Lite-S classifications and performance hold under independent annotation or a larger benchmark?
I inspected the method, selected results and analysis pages, but not the full paper's appendices or implementation details; reproducibility and sensitivity beyond the reported setup remain uncertain.
